procedural_matters: At the beginning of the hearing Julia Schmidt and Louis Mayo (members of the international jury panel) declared that they saw the incident and gave evidence as witnesses.
USA 43 did not come to the hearing, the hearing proceeded in accordance with RRS 63.1(b).
facts: After race 5, Mr. Ramon Olicen (support person 205) was motoring the rib with a speed of approximately 5 knots, into the direction of the race committee signal vessel, with the kill cord line dangling from the throttle.
After waving at the jury vessel, Mr. Ramon Olicen reached down to the kill cord line and attached it to his leg.
During the hearing Mr. Ramon Olicen admitted that he was not wearing the kill cord and apologized.
conclusions: By not wearing the kill cord while the engine was running, Mr. Ramon Olicen broke ESTR 3.2.
Using the World Sailing Discretionary Penalty Guidelines for Boats and Support Persons a starting penalty of level 2 was decided.
Although the breach could have affected safety, the support person was apologetic and promptly remedied the breach; the level 2 will hence stand.
decision: Mr. Ramon Olicen shall stay ashore until the first race of their supported boat(s) on June 23rd has started.
